2025_300_mscurrguide_24_25_42.paragraph: Troy School District's Middle School Curriculum Guide for 2024-2025 states the district's middle school philosophy, nine program goals, five graduate outcomes, and the complete course catalog for grades 6, 7 and 8. Sixth graders take five academic classes plus required every-other-day physical education, while seventh and eighth graders take four academic classes plus required half-year Health/Physical Education and Digital Applications 1.0. Algebra 1 Honors, Geometry Honors and World Language I are taken in eighth grade, each earning high school credit and counting toward the high school GPA. **Publication**
Troy School District Middle School Curriculum Guide, 2024-2025, 18 pages, presented to the Board of Education on February 11, 2025.

**Philosophy and Goals**
Troy middle schools provide a program that recognizes, accepts, respects and meets the diverse needs of young adolescents, characterized by a research-based curriculum with effective assessment and evaluation; a shared vision fostering respect for learning, diversity and responsible behavior; and a cooperative partnership with parents and community. Nine goals are listed, covering developmentally appropriate programs, meeting the needs of a diverse student population, core-subject skills and knowledge, discovery of special interests and aptitudes, diversified cultural/social/civic/vocational/recreational experiences, guidance services promoting self-esteem and responsible behavior, community partnerships, transition from elementary to high school, and modeling healthy lifestyles.

**Outcomes**
Five student outcomes: a self-directed learner, a quality worker, a positive communicator, a collaborative and cooperative contributor, and an involved and visionary citizen.

**Three-Year Overview**

| Grade | Academic load | Additional requirements |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | Five academic classes | Physical Education EOD required; music students may add Orchestra EOD, Choir EOD, Band EOD, Art EOD |
| 7 | Four academic classes | Health/Physical Education half year; Digital Applications 1.0 half year; music option of Concert Band, Chamber Orchestra or Choir full year; elective total of one full year |
| 8 | Four academic classes | Music option of Symphonic Band, Advanced Orchestra or Choir full year; elective total of one full year for music students, two full-year classes for non-music students |

EOD is defined as Every Other Day.

**Grade 6 Courses**
Required: ELA 6, Language Arts 6, Mathematics 6 (or another math class), Physical Education 6, Science 6, Social Studies 6. Mathematics 6 is organized into ten units: Area and Surface Area; Introducing Ratios; Linear Relationships; Unit Rates and Percentages; Dividing Fractions; Arithmetic in Base Ten; Expressions and Equations; Rational Numbers; Data Sets and Distributions; Putting it all Together. Grade 6 electives meet every other day alternating with PE: Art 6, Band 6 or Orchestra 6, and 6th Grade Choir.

**Grade 7 Courses**
Digital Applications 1.0 (half year, required), English 7, Health and Physical Education 7 (half year, a ten-week course covering nutrition, recognizing influences, human sexuality and choosing healthy behaviors, with parental excusal permitted), Mathematics 7, Science 7, and Social Studies 7, which surveys ancient world history and geography from the beginning until around 1500.

**Grade 8 Courses**
Algebra 1 Honors (five critical areas), English 8, Geometry Honors (six critical areas), Mathematics 8, Science 8, and United States History 8, which surveys U.S. history from the time of the Native Americans to 1877. Algebra 1 Honors and Geometry Honors count toward high school credit and the high school GPA.

**Electives**
Half-year electives for grades 7 and 8: 2D Visual Art, 3D Visual Art, Applied Engineering, Art Expressions, Ceramics, Communication Arts, Computer Programming, Computer Science Discoveries, Creation Lab, Digital Applications 2.0, Innovation Incubator, Life Skills, LINKS (teacher recommendation only), Money Matters, Science and Engineering Explorations, Theatre Arts, Video Technology, and Video Technology 2. Grade 7 full-year electives: Chamber Orchestra, Choir 7, 7th/8th Choir, Concert Band, Graphic Design/Yearbook. Grade 8 electives: 7th/8th Choir, Advanced Orchestra, Choir 8, Fundamentals of Fitness, Graphic Design/Yearbook, Jazz Band, Physical Education, Symphonic Band, WEB Leadership, and World Language I in Chinese I, French I, German I, Japanese I and Spanish I.
2025_300_mscurrguide_24_25_42.verbose:
The Troy School District Middle School Curriculum Guide for 2024-2025 is an 18-page publication appearing on the Board of Education agenda of February 11, 2025. It opens with the district's middle school philosophy: Troy middle schools provide a program that creates an environment recognizing, accepting, respecting and meeting the diverse needs and characteristics of young adolescent students, committed to academic excellence and to being developmentally responsive to adolescents' innate curiosity, desire to expand their environment, and need for recognition and personal achievement. The program is characterized by a research-based curriculum with effective assessment and evaluation that is challenging, integrative and exploratory; a shared vision with all members of the educational community fostering respect for learning, diversity and responsible behavior; and a cooperative partnership with parents and community members.

Nine Middle School Goals are enumerated. Goal 1: all programs will be developmentally appropriate. Goal 2: ensure all programs meet the needs of a diverse student population. Goal 3: ensure all students develop skills and knowledge in the core subject areas. Goal 4: provide opportunity to discover special interests, attitudes, aptitudes and abilities. Goal 5: provide diversified experiences in cultural, social, civic, vocational and recreational programs. Goal 6: provide guidance services and programs promoting self-esteem, independence and responsible behavior. Goal 7: provide opportunity to establish partnerships with the community. Goal 8: provide a transition from elementary to high school. Goal 9: provide a model for healthy lifestyles.

Five Middle School Outcomes follow: a self-directed learner who is responsible, enthusiastic, thinks independently and is open-minded and intellectually curious; a quality worker who designs a plan, applies resources, technologies and organizational strategies, creates products and performances, monitors development, maintains high standards and assesses results; a positive communicator; a collaborative and cooperative contributor who creates and sustains productive group relationships, respects the contributions of others, helps resolve conflicts and stays focused and task oriented; and an involved and visionary citizen who develops awareness of global issues, contributes to local and world communities, advocates for the environment and prepares to meet future challenges.

The three-year middle school overview specifies that all sixth graders take five academic classes; seventh and eighth graders each take four academic classes. Sixth grade requires Physical Education on an every-other-day (EOD) basis for both music and non-music students, with Orchestra EOD, Choir EOD, Band EOD and Art EOD listed as the alternating options. Seventh grade requires Health/Physical Education for a half year and Digital Applications 1.0 for a half year, plus, for music students, one of Concert Band (full year), Chamber Orchestra (full year) or Choir (full year); the elective load totals one full year, taken as two half-year classes or one full-year class. Eighth grade music students choose among Symphonic Band (full year), Advanced Orchestra (full year) and Choir (full year); non-music eighth graders carry an elective total of two full-year classes, taken as four half-year classes, two half-year classes plus one full-year class, or two full-year classes.

Grade 6 required courses are ELA 6 (full year), which studies literature of various genres and informational text including literary nonfiction with emphasis on inference from textual evidence, thematic and character development, claims and evidence, academic vocabulary and independent choice reading; Language Arts 6 (full year), covering narrative, informational and argumentative writing using mentor texts and the writing process; Mathematics 6 (full year, or another math class), covering ratio and rate, dividing fractions by fractions, negative numbers and variables; Physical Education 6 (full year EOD), run either as a yearlong every-other-day program or an everyday semester class; Science 6 (full year), with units on cells and heredity, ecology, Earth's changing surface, and species adaptation and survival; and Social Studies 6 (full year), a geography-based course covering physical and human geography, migration and settlement, culture and cultural diffusion, population and demographic changes, resource use, and trade and economic interdependence. Mathematics 6 lists ten units: Unit 1 Area and Surface Area; Unit 2 Introducing Ratios; Unit 3 Linear Relationships; Unit 4 Unit Rates and Percentages; Unit 5 Dividing Fractions; Unit 6 Arithmetic in Base Ten; Unit 7 Expressions and Equations; Unit 8 Rational Numbers; Unit 9 Data Sets and Distributions; Unit 10 Putting it all Together.

Grade 6 elective courses meet every other day, alternating with PE: Art 6 (full year EOD), Band 6 or Orchestra 6 (full year EOD, with fifth-grade band or orchestra or prior formal instruction expected), and 6th Grade Choir (full year EOD), which follows the National Core Arts Standards of Perform, Create, Respond and Connect.

Grade 7 required courses are Digital Applications 1.0 (half year), covering 21st Century and Web 2.0 online tools; English 7 (full year); Health and Physical Education 7 (half year), a combined ten-week course covering nutrition, recognizing influences, human sexuality and choosing healthy behaviors, with units countering messages encouraging tobacco, alcohol and other drug use and information on the spread of AIDS and sexually transmitted diseases, and with parents permitted to excuse their child from sessions on human sexuality and AIDS; Mathematics 7 (full year, or another math class), extending rates and ratios to proportional relationships and all rational numbers; Science 7 (full year), covering Earth's waters, weather and climate, astronomy, waves, energy, physical and chemical changes, and chemical properties; and Social Studies 7 (full year), focused on ancient world history and geography with content literacy, investigating human history from the beginning until around 1500.

Grade 8 courses are Algebra 1 Honors (full year, or another math class), a first-year high school algebra course for advanced students with five critical areas covering linear equations and inequalities, functions and sequences, regression techniques, exponential/quadratic/rational equations and systems, and specialized functions including absolute value, step and piecewise-defined; English 8 (full year); Geometry Honors (full year, or another math class) for advanced students who have completed Algebra 1 Honors, with six critical areas covering congruence and rigid motions, similarity and right triangle trigonometry, coordinate geometry, circles, geometric measurement in two and three dimensions, and geometric modeling; Mathematics 8 (full year, or another math class), covering linear relationships, linear equations in one and two variables, functions and irrational numbers; Science 8 (full year), covering energy, biogeochemical cycles, resources and human impacts, the rock cycle, Earth's interior, plate tectonics, earthquakes, volcanoes, hydrogeology, severe weather, Earth in space, the sun, Earth history and geologic time and climate change, including an online Moodle project; and United States History 8 (full year), surveying U.S. history from the time of the Native Americans to 1877, with detailed study of the American Revolution, formation of the national government, westward movement, and the Civil War and Reconstruction, and periodic study of Michigan history and U.S. foreign affairs. Both Algebra 1 Honors and Geometry Honors count toward high school credit and are figured into the high school GPA.

Half-year elective courses for grades 7 and 8 are 2D Visual Art; 3D Visual Art (papier-mache, clay, batik and mixed media); Applied Engineering (stress analysis, mechanical engineering, renewable energy systems, aerodynamics, space and rocketry); Art Expressions; Ceramics (pinch, coil and slab construction); Communication Arts (public speaking, pantomime, roleplaying, interviews, listening skills, improvisation); Computer Programming (Introduction to JavaScript: Drawing and Animation, JavaScript: Games and Visualizations, HTML/CSS: Making Webpages, HTML/JS: Making Webpages Interactive, plus building and programming a robot); Computer Science Discoveries; Creation Lab (bridge building, soldering, coding, game creation, projectiles, S.T.E.A.M. focus); Digital Applications 2.0 (Adobe Creative Suite, video production, animation, digital imaging, Dreamweaver; prerequisite is successful completion of Digital Applications 1.0); Innovation Incubator, whose cornerstone is the Larson Innovation Shark Tank project in which teams pitch inventions to members of the Metro Detroit business community including market researchers, patent attorneys and engineers; Life Skills (food preparation and hand and machine sewing); LINKS, a peer-to-peer support program pairing general education students with students with Autism Spectrum Disorder and other special needs, by teacher recommendation only; Money Matters (Michigan Career Pathways, budgets, bank accounts, credit, interest, investing and responsible spending); Science and Engineering Explorations, which prepares work for competitions such as the Science and Engineering Fair of Metro Detroit (SEFMD); Theatre Arts, which includes a public performance; Video Technology, using Windows Movie Maker and Apple iMovie with live morning news broadcasts and media literacy and copyright ethics; and Video Technology 2.

Grade 7 full-year electives are Chamber Orchestra, Choir 7, 7th/8th Choir, Concert Band, and Graphic Design/Yearbook, the latter connecting students with the Boulan Park School Community. Grade 8 electives are 7th/8th Choir, Advanced Orchestra (which requires many evening performances plus a Saturday performance at the MSBOA Orchestra Festival), Choir 8, Fundamentals of Fitness, Graphic Design/Yearbook, Jazz Band (by audition or teacher approval, with members also participating in a concert band ensemble), Physical Education, Symphonic Band (requiring many evening performances plus two Saturday performances including MSBOA Band Festival), WEB Leadership (Where Everyone Belongs, covering sixth grade orientation, school character and culture programs, charity opportunities and student mentoring), and World Language I. World Language I is a full-year, every-day course counting toward high school credit and the high school GPA, offered in Chinese I, French I, German I, Japanese I and Spanish I; the guide warns the class may only be offered at the high school during 1st hour, that parents would need to provide transportation to the high school, and that a shuttle will bring students back to the middle school.

**Understanding School Funding (2024-25)**
The foundation allowance is built from state aid, a Non-Homestead Levy of $2,804 per pupil, and a Hold-Harmless Levy of $786 per pupil, with the amount dependent upon voter approval given as $3,590. Highlights: contractual obligation reconciled; projected $1.2 million use of fund balance; projected $2.4 million fund balance; $1.6 million remaining excess fund balance; $1.4 million set to be spent on Troy High Kitchen.

**Other Ancillary Fund Highlights**
Community Service Fund: projected $(278k) operating deficit, projected $1.8 million fund balance, and a reminder of no Federal Childcare Stabilization funds in FY2025. Preschool Fund: $95k projected operating surplus, $2.3 million projected fund balance, Universal Preschool as the Governor's initiative for 25-26, and no Federal Childcare Stabilization funds in FY2025. TCC Fund: revenues equal expenditures. Sinking Fund: $433k projected operating surplus and $509k projected fund balance.

2025_305_feb_2025_financial_statement.paragraph: Troy School District's monthly financial report for the period July 1, 2024 through February 28, 2025 (unaudited) presents statements of revenues and expenditures for the General Fund, Consolidated Debt Service Funds, four special revenue funds, the Sinking Fund and two capital projects funds, each measured against the amended budget adopted March 18, 2025.
